hints.content:
The equation is in *slope-intercept form* : $y=m\!\cdot\!x+b$. In this form, $m$ gives us the slope of the line and $b$ gives us its $y$-intercept.

So $y=-\dfrac{3}{2}x-3$ has a slope of $-\dfrac{3}{2}$ and a $y$-intercept at $(0,-3)$.

We need two points. We already have the $y$-intercept $(0,-3)$.

We can find a second point by reasoning about the slope. A slope of $-\dfrac{3 }{2 }$ means that when the $x$-value increases by $\purple{ 2}$, the $y$-value decreases by $\green{3 }$.

$(0 \purple{+2},-3 \green{-3})=(2,-6)$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The points zero, negative three and two, six are plotted. There is a horizontal segment from zero, negative three to two, negative three that is labeled plus two. There is a vertical segment from two, negative three to two, negative six that is labeled minus three.
